title: Activepieces vs MuleSoft: Cost and Features (2026)
summary: Activepieces vs MuleSoft: choose MuleSoft for enterprise API governance or Activepieces for automation you host yourself or embed in your product.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


### Scope and licence


Plans and terms change, so confirm each against the vendor page named below before you sign; the answers reflect what we reviewed on 30 October 2026. These are the questions the body leaves open.


Can Activepieces replace MuleSoft? It can for workflow automation between business systems, but not for an enterprise-wide API program. If your need is governed API design, a central catalogue and a dedicated integration team, MuleSoft's Anypoint Platform covers that and Activepieces doesn't aim to.


Is Activepieces really open source? The core is open source under the MIT licence, and you can self-host it. Enterprise features are under a commercial licence, so check which features your plan needs before assuming everything is free to run.


SSO beyond the Team plan, self-hosted enterprise and embedding go through the sales form at[https://www.activepieces.com/sales](https://www.activepieces.com/sales) .


### Security and compliance


Does Activepieces have SOC 2? No. The SOC 2 programme is in progress, and Activepieces doesn't hold a certification today. If your procurement checklist requires a report, treat it as a gap and ask sales for the current status in writing.


### Using both and sizing


Can I use both together? Yes. Keep MuleSoft as the governed API layer for core systems, and let individual teams build lighter workflows on top of those APIs.


The adoption pattern to plan for is that a department automates first and central IT governs afterward, so name an owner for the connections that cross the boundary.


Is MuleSoft overkill for a small team? Usually, if your goal is a handful of automations. MuleSoft's entry plan is published on its pricing page, but anything beyond it is quoted by sales, so you can't budget for growth from public information alone.


Compare that with the Activepieces self-serve plans at[https://www.activepieces.com/pricing](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) , where you can see the cost before talking to anyone.


Self-hosting alone doesn't separate the two, since MuleSoft does support running in your own infrastructure through customer-hosted runtimes. The difference is how much platform you must adopt to get it. Confirm the exact deployment options with MuleSoft before committing.
